name: Blenheim
note: Town: the largest town and transport hub of the Marlborough region, a base for the wineries and the Omaka museum.

name: Picton
note: Town: port town and car-ferry gateway to the Marlborough Sounds, with a waterfront and museums.

name: Havelock
note: Town: green-lipped mussel town and access point to the Pelorus Sound.

name: Renwick
note: Town: satellite town to Blenheim, with the South Marlborough DOC office and several wineries nearby.

name: Seddon
note: Town: small town south of the Awatere River on State Highway 1, a stop between Blenheim and Kaikoura.

name: Ward
note: Town: small settlement in the Flaxbourne district, on State Highway 1; Ward Beach is nearby.

name: Rai Valley
note: Settlement: rural village and link route to the western Marlborough Sounds.

name: Waikawa Bay
note: Bay and suburb of Picton: the main yacht and powerboat marina, with a walk to Karaka Point.

name: Anakiwa
note: Settlement: the finishing point of the Queen Charlotte Track in the Grove Arm, reached by water taxi or track.

name: Okiwi Bay
note: Bay: a Marlborough Sounds bay with DOC lookout and valley walks, reached by road or boat.

name: Ngākuta Bay
note: Bay: Marlborough Sounds bay named in the Marlborough District article; no visitor source found yet.

name: Elaine Bay
note: Bay: Pelorus Sound bay with a DOC campsite; the Tui Nature Reserve eco-boat tours leave from it (listed on Wikivoyage Marlborough Sounds).

name: Marlborough Sounds
note: Area: a series of drowned valleys (sounds) at the northern end of the region; a destination-level area, not a single spot.

name: Queen Charlotte Sound
note: Sound: the arm of the Marlborough Sounds nearest Picton, crossed by the Queen Charlotte Track and cruises from Picton.

name: Pelorus Sound
note: Sound: the western arm of the Marlborough Sounds, reached from Havelock; a sound with DOC tracks and campsites, not a single spot.

name: Kenepuru Sound
note: Sound: the inner arm reached by Queen Charlotte Drive from Havelock, with commanding views and DOC campsites.

name: Queen Charlotte Drive
note: Scenic road: narrow, windy drive with views over the Kenepuru and inner Queen Charlotte sounds; a drive, not a spot, unless judged a stop in itself.

name: French Pass
note: Settlement and strait: the narrow French Pass between D'Urville Island and the mainland, with a lookout track and campsite.

name: D'Urville Island
note: Island: large island at the northern end of the Sounds, with scenic reserves; limited visitor infrastructure (marginal).

name: Queen Charlotte Track
note: Multi-day walk: the 3-4 day track (about 70 km) from Ship Cove to Anakiwa, also walkable or bikeable as day sections.

name: Ship Cove
note: Historic site: Meretoto / Ship Cove, where Captain Cook spent the most time on his voyages, with a memorial at the start of the Queen Charlotte Track.

name: Motuara Island
note: Island: scenic reserve in Queen Charlotte Sound with a lookout track and historic Cook memorial site.

name: Blumine Island
note: Island: scenic reserve in Queen Charlotte Sound (Oruawairua) with a track and campsite.

name: Nydia Track
note: Walk: a 2-day track between Kaiuma Bay and Duncan Bay in Tennyson Inlet, reached by water taxi or mail boat from Havelock.

name: Havelock Museum
note: Museum: local-history museum on Main Road in Havelock.

name: Rutherford and Pickering Memorial
note: Memorial: plaque-style memorial on Main Road, Havelock, to two scientists educated locally (minor memorial).

name: Greenshell Mussel Cruise
note: Operator cruise: 3-hour sounds cruise from Havelock Marina that visits a mussel farm; the cruise is the vehicle, the mussel farm the place (operator-level).

name: Beachcomber Mail Boat
note: Operator cruise: Picton mail boat delivering to Marlborough Sounds bays; the vehicle, not a place (operator-level).

name: Edwin Fox Maritime Museum
note: Museum: the Edwin Fox, an 1853 ship (one of the oldest in the world) being restored on the Picton foreshore.

name: Picton Heritage & Whaling Museum
note: Museum: Māori, maritime and whaling artefacts on London Quay, next to Memorial Park.

name: Picton Model Engineers
note: Model railway: elevated model railway and boat pond on the foreshore, open Sundays, school holidays and public holidays only (recurring, not every day).

name: Karaka Point
note: Walk and lookout: 10-minute walk from Waikawa Bay car park past a former Māori pā to a lookout and stony beach.

name: Snout Walkway
note: Walk: a bush-covered peninsula between Picton and Waikawa Bay with tracks from a few minutes to 3.5 hours, free.

name: Tui Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: Tui Nature Reserve in the outer Pelorus Sound, reached by eco-boat tour from Havelock or Elaine Bay (the reserve is the place; the tour is the vehicle).

name: Bay of Many Coves
wiki: Bay of Many Coves / Mirituu Bay
note: Bay: Queen Charlotte Sound bay on the Queen Charlotte Track, mainly known for its DOC campsite.

name: Momorangi Forest Experience Walk
note: Walk: short forest walk in the Queen Charlotte Sound near Momorangi Bay.

name: Governors Bay Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Queen Charlotte Sound/Tōtaranui area.

name: Kumutoto Bay Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Queen Charlotte Sound/Tōtaranui area to Kumutoto Bay.

name: Mistletoe Bay Tracks
note: Walk: DOC tracks around Mistletoe Bay in the Queen Charlotte Sound.

name: Antimony Mines Track
note: Walk: DOC track to historic antimony mine workings in the Queen Charlotte Sound.

name: Cullen Point Tracks
note: Walk: DOC tracks to Cullen Point in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Putanui Point Track
note: Walk: DOC track to Putanui Point in the Kenepuru Sound area.

name: Piwakawaka Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Archer Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Ferndale Tracks
note: Walk: DOC tracks at Ferndale in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Mount Stokes Track
note: Walk: DOC track to Mount Stokes in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Opouri Bridle Track
note: Walk: DOC bridle track in the Pelorus and Kenepuru sounds area.

name: Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve
note: Scenic reserve: forested reserve on the Pelorus River with river swimming, tracks and a campsite.

name: Tōtara Walk
note: Walk: DOC walk through tōtara forest in Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve.

name: Elvy Waterfalls Track
note: Walk: DOC track to the Elvy waterfalls in Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve.

name: Circle Walk
note: Walk: DOC loop walks in Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve.

name: Tawa and Weta Walks
note: Walk: DOC walks in Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve.

name: Trig K Track
note: Walk: DOC track in Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve to a trig point.

name: Mount Richmond Forest Park
note: Park: forest park in the Richmond Ranges, with walks, tramping routes and huts; the Te Araroa route runs through it.

name: Forks Riverside Walk
note: Walk: DOC riverside walk at the Forks in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Richmond Ranges Te Araroa Route
note: Long trail: the Te Araroa national trail section through the Richmond Ranges.

name: Pelorus Track
note: Tramping track: DOC track in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Mount Sunday and Mount Riley Track
note: Tramping track: DOC route to Mount Sunday and Mount Riley in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Old Man Hut Circuit
note: Tramping circuit: DOC circuit around the Old Man hut in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Lake Chalice
note: Lake and tramping tracks: alpine lake in Mount Richmond Forest Park reached by DOC tracks and a hut.

name: Hacket Track
note: Tramping track: DOC track in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Wakamarina Track
note: Tramping track: DOC track in the Wakamarina area of Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Waikakahocullen Creek Track
note: Tramping track: DOC track in Mount Richmond Forest Park.

name: Mount Robertson Tramping Tracks
note: Tramping tracks: DOC tracks on Mount Robertson near Blenheim.

name: Wither Hills Farm Park
note: Farm park: hills framing Blenheim to the south, with walking and mountain-biking tracks and views over the Wairau Valley.

name: Wither Hills Bike Park
note: Mountain-bike park: trail park within the Wither Hills, Blenheim.

name: Black Jack Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Blenheim area.

name: Monkey Bay Walk
note: Walk: DOC coastal walk in the Blenheim area.

name: Pukaka Valley Track
note: Walk: DOC valley track in the Blenheim area.

name: Pukatea Walk
note: Walk: DOC short walk in the Blenheim area.

name: Wairau Lagoons
note: Wetland and walkway: lagoons at the Wairau River mouth, a birdwatching walk near Blenheim.

name: Whites Bay
note: Bay and track: Rarangi–Whites Bay Track to a bay on the coast north of Blenheim, with a campsite.

name: Ward Beach
note: Beach: beach named in the Marlborough District article; no visitor-oriented source found yet.

name: Cloudy Bay
note: Bay: Te Koko-o-Kupe / Cloudy Bay on the south-east coast; not confirmed as a visitor stop (distinct from Cloudy Bay Vineyards).

name: Okiwi Bay Seaward Valley Track
note: Walk: DOC track from Okiwi Bay into the Seaward Valley.

name: Patutu Route
note: Tramping route: DOC route in the Okiwi Bay area.

name: Marfells Beach
note: Beach: remote beach on the east coast leading to Cape Campbell, with a DOC campsite.

name: Cape Campbell Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: historic lighthouse at Cape Campbell, reached by the Marfells Beach to Cape Campbell route; public access is limited (check).

name: Lake Grassmere
note: Lake and salt works: a salt lake between Seddon and Ward on State Highway 1, with salt pans and bird life.

name: Molesworth Station
note: High-country station and reserve: Molesworth Recreation Reserve, reached by the Acheron Road, with lookouts, huts and campsites.

name: Molesworth Homestead Lookout Track
note: Walk: DOC lookout track at Molesworth Station.

name: Acheron Lookout Loop Walk
note: Walk: DOC lookout loop in the Molesworth Recreation Reserve.

name: Trig Lookout Track (Mount Chisholm)
note: Walk: DOC lookout track to a trig in the Molesworth Recreation Reserve.

name: Pudding Hill Track
note: Walk: DOC track in the Molesworth Recreation Reserve.

name: Mount Augarde Track
note: Tramping track: DOC track in the Molesworth Recreation Reserve.

name: Acheron Road
note: Scenic 4WD road: the unsealed road through Molesworth Station, a drive rather than a stop (marginal).

name: Lake Tennyson
note: Lake: high-country lake in the Molesworth Recreation Reserve, known through its DOC campsite.

name: Rainbow Road
note: Road: unsealed high-country route from Hanmer Springs to St Arnaud across the Molesworth reserve (a drive, marginal). Views zeroed: the name matches an unrelated article.

name: Sawcut Gorge
note: Gorge: a narrow limestone gorge in the Marlborough high country, named by Wikivoyage as a tramping secret.

name: Rainbow Skifield
note: Ski area: seasonal ski field near St Arnaud, listed by Wikivoyage under Marlborough (it may sit in Tasman; check).

name: Pollard Park
note: Park: central Blenheim park known for its rose and camellia gardens.

name: Seymour Square
note: Square: formal gardens in central Blenheim.

name: Millennium Art Gallery
note: Gallery: public art gallery on Seymour Street in Blenheim, free with donation.

name: Marlborough Museum
note: Museum: local-history museum in Brayshaw Museum Park, with the Beavertown replica village.

name: Omaka Aviation Heritage Centre
note: Museum: World War I and II aircraft restored and displayed in realistic settings, made with Peter Jackson and Weta Workshop.

name: Hedgerows Strawberry Farm
note: Farm: strawberry farm between Blenheim and Renwick selling fresh fruit and ice cream, with a petanque court and picnic areas.

name: Mud House Village
note: Cellar door and village: wine and coffee tasting with an olive shop and craft barn on Rapaura Road.

name: Cloudy Bay Vineyards
note: Winery cellar door: Jacksons Road winery known for its Sauvignon Blanc and sparkling wines.

name: Highfield Estate
note: Winery cellar door: Brookby Road winery with a tower giving views over the lower Wairau River (summer hours).

name: Hunters Wines
note: Winery cellar door: Rapaura Road winery with a restaurant and native garden.

name: Brancott Estate
note: Winery cellar door: the large visitor facility on Brancott Road, with restaurant and theatre.

name: Nautilus Estate
note: Winery cellar door: Rapaura Road winery known for its Cuvée sparkling wine.

name: Seresin Estate
note: Winery cellar door: organic vineyard on Bedford Road, Renwick, with views over Condors Bend.

name: Villa Maria Estate
note: Winery cellar door: award-winning winery at Paynters and New Renwick roads, with free tastings.

name: Marlborough Wine Region
note: Wine region: New Zealand's largest wine area, with over 35 cellar doors, best visited by bike or tour from Blenheim (a region, not a spot).

name: Long Island-Kokomohua Marine Reserve
note: Marine reserve: no-take marine reserve in the Marlborough Sounds, named in the Marlborough District article; no visitor source found yet.

name: Stephens Island Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: on predator-free Stephens Island, a nature reserve closed to the public (likely fails access).

name: Maud Island
